decision: Do not adopt into production: pointer maps repair fresh-allocation random reads but fragmented free-page reuse restores amplification; sequential reads regress and aggressive mostly-live compaction raises GC cost. Live-slice reclamation is correct.

limitations: VFS bytes describe SQLite software I/O, not physical SSD traffic; OS caches stay enabled.
Shared host, all samples and stalls retained; no external filesystem rerun.
GC compacts every partial extent in one write transaction; no work or lock-duration budget.
Pointer-map read optimization guesses consecutive overflow pages and may fall back on fragmented allocation.
Sequential read uses the existing per-block incremental BLOB calls; no coalescing or cross-transaction BLOB cache.
Fresh databases enable INCREMENTAL pointer maps; existing unmapped experimental databases are not migrated.
No incremental_vacuum call: freed SQLite pages remain reusable and file length may not shrink.
